answer: Forced-Divergence Challenge Ledger. Each identity must periodically answer a randomly seeded challenge whose accepted answer depends on its full interaction history, so two clones holding identical state cannot both pass: any divergence to satisfy different seeds permanently forks their records. The ledger stores the fork as a tundra of unmatched hashes, flagging both copies. An attacker cloning N agents pays N distinct maintenance streams, since shared state collapses under the pigment of conflicting responses. Detection cost scales with copies, not with a canyon of separate audits.
